result.note: Tests the body that opened the SEZ domestic-sales window and the window's conditions (cap, value addition, duration).

questions.prompt: In March 2026, which body opened a one-year window for Special Economic Zone (SEZ) manufacturers to sell goods into the domestic market at concessional customs duty rates?
options: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
questions.explain: The Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) opened the window, citing global trade disruptions. It lets SEZ units clear goods into the Domestic Tariff Area at reduced duty rates.
questions.source: the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) opened a one-year window for Special Economic Zone (SEZ) manufacturers to sell goods into the domestic market at concessional customs duty rates

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the concessional window for SEZ units to sell into the Domestic Tariff Area, opened in March 2026:
items: Domestic sales are capped at 30% of a unit's best export year over the previous three financial years.
Goods must have at least 20% value addition over inputs.
The window runs for two years, until 31 March 2028.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 3 is wrong: the window is for one year, from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027. Only units operational by 31 March 2025 qualify, and sensitive sectors are excluded entirely.
questions.source: Domestic sales are capped at 30% of a unit's best export year over the previous three financial years.
